## The multiplier

AI writes most of the first drafts. I set the direction, keep the context in order, and review everything before it ships. Every project starts as a spec and a rules file, so the agents build to a plan.

<table>
<tr><th align="left" width="50%">Toolkit</th><th align="left" width="50%">The loop</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">
<b>Claude Code</b>: main driver: parallel sessions, one per workstream<br>
<b>Cursor</b>: in-editor edits and fast refactors<br>
<b>Cline</b>: agentic tasks inside VS Code<br>
<b>MCP</b>: agents wired into docs, data and services<br>
<b>LLM APIs</b>: RAG, embeddings and generation inside the products themselves
</td><td valign="top">
1. <code>SPEC.md</code> product spec and designs<br>
2. <code>CLAUDE.md</code> house rules: stack, style, limits<br>
3. <code>MEMORY + REGISTRY</code> agents keep a map of features and files<br>
4. <code>parallel agents</code> one per platform or feature<br>
5. <code>review + ship</code> I read every diff before it merges
</td></tr>
</table>
